what_its_for: Alpelisib is a cancer medicine (called a PI3K inhibitor) used to treat certain types of breast cancer in adults that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is used along with another medicine called fulvestrant. It works by blocking a protein in cancer cells that helps them grow and multiply, which can slow or stop the cancer from spreading.
how_to_take: Take alpelisib by mouth once a day WITH a meal. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Take it at the same time each day. Drink plenty of water throughout the day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another tablet that day — just take your next scheduled dose the following day.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 300 mg (two 150 mg tablets) taken once daily with food. Your doctor may lower your dose to 250 mg or 200 mg if you have side effects. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 9 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember with food. If it has been MORE than 9 hours, skip that dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store alpelisib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice, as it may increase the amount of this medicine in your blood and cause more side effects. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, as it can make alpelisib less effective. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements. Avoid high-sugar foods and drinks, as this medicine can raise your blood sugar. Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose, because this drug can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling skin (even inside your mouth); signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, headache, or blurred vision; severe diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting; mouth sores that are very painful or make it hard to eat or drink; shortness of breath or a new cough (which could be a sign of lung problems); swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; signs of low blood cell counts such as unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, or chills. Do not wait — some of these side effects can be serious and need prompt medical attention.
when_it_works: Alpelisib does not cure cancer, but it can help slow the growth or spread of cancer cells. Most patients do not feel it working right away. Your doctor will check your progress with regular blood tests, imaging scans, and office visits. It is important to keep taking the medicine every day as directed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use alpelisib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm your unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Older adults (age 65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects such as high blood sugar, diarrhea, and decreased appetite. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Diabetes: Tell your doctor if you have diabetes or take medicines that lower blood sugar, because alpelisib can raise blood sugar and your diabetes treatment may need to be changed.
